title.narrative: Output 4.2. Strengthened capacity of enterprises and their support systems to enhance productivity and sustainability

description.narrative: The ILO’s tripartite constituents made significant progress towards supporting private sector development and job creation. In March 2023, the government of Iraq launched the "Riyada initiative" to support SMEs start-ups with focus on unemployed youth through capacity building and access to finance. Within this framework, capacities of 100 trainers from 36 entities including the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (MOLSA) and the Ministry of Youth and Sports, financial institutions, chambers and local BDS providers were enhanced to provide continuous entrepreneurship and financial education trainings using the ILO SIYB and financial education programmes (a total of 2100 youth and businesses trained from various governorates). As such, both MOLSA's and MOYS's allocated budget lines to build capacity of vocational and youth training center by training trainers to deliver entrepreneurship and financial education for youth and businesses to support their start-up and growth. Additionally, the Central bank of Iraq and Al Thiqa MFI expanded the implementation of innovative financial inclusion models in commercial banks and MFIs. A pilot framework was adopted and is replicable to expand access to finance in Iraq. Access to finance expanded to refugees in addition of IDPs and HCs. Financial institutions including banks, ICBG, MFI and Central bank of Iraq strengthened their delivery of MSMEs finance. - Financial inclusion efforts are practically put in place in three selected commercial banks and MFI and loans provided for 850 entrepreneurs, also access to finance expanded to refugees in addition of IDPs and HC s through MF institution in Dohuk and Ninewa. With the support of the Government of Netherlands, Germany, European Union, and IOM, the ILO has provided technical support to realize the results: Through its innovative financial inclusion models, the ILO supported capacity strengthening of Central bank of Iraq, ICBG and 3 partner banks and several MFIs to pilot new innovative products to serve MSMEs including youth start-ups, refugees, and IDPs in addition to HC members. A pilot intervention supported by PROSPECTS has benefited a total of 923 loans disbursed for the value of 3.35 million USD leading to 2,422 jobs being created and sustained. Using ILO tools "Start and Improve Your Business," and "Financial Education (FE)," the ILO built the capacities of 100 trainers from 36 entities including ministries, chambers, BDS providers and financial institutions. It also used "Making Finance Work for Refugees," to strengthen the capacities of 18 staff from the Central Bank of Iraq, the Iraqi Company for Bank Guarantees, Iraqi commercial banks (Cihan Bank, Middle East Investment), a microfinance institution, Al Thiqa, to deliver financial products for vulnerable groups. These trainers have reached a total of 2,100 Iraqi potential entrepreneurs, start-ups and existing businesses under the framework of PROSPECTS support with at least 40% women participation rates. ILO trained a total of 96 trainers (23 women) from 21 private, public and partner business service provider organizations, on the SIYB and FE programme. The trainers in turn trained a total of 1581 (810 women) entrepreneurs across KRI (Duhok, Erbil, Halabja, Kalar, Khanqin, Mosul, Soran, Sulaymaniyah and Zakho) in 2022.The ILO conducted two on-line refresher and coaching sessions for 50 trainers from IOM. 40 (IOM) staff members are certified as ILO/SIYB trainers. entrepreneurs across Iraq. 1,000 beneficiaries (refugees, IDPs, and vulnerable host communities) benefited from the SIYB training.
